notices.short_title: Integrated Support Hotels Program
notices.description:
The Department of Homeless Services  is seeking appropriately qualified contractors or vendors to contract for the provision of shelter services for families with children, adult families, and single adults who are temporarily housed in DHS contracted commercial hotels. The selected vendors will provide services as outlined in this RFP to assist clients with their daily needs and to help them move out of the shelter system as quickly as possible. DHS will continue to need commercial hotel capacity to meet the legally mandated requirement to provide shelter. 

Sites:
Myrtle Emergency Shelter 1090 Myrtle Avenue Brooklyn NY 11206. 87 units.
802 Hotel 802 Flushing Avenue Brooklyn NY 11206. 63 units.
notices.plain: The Department of Homeless Services awarded Bronx Parent Housing Network Inc. a $43.95 million contract to provide services for families and single adults housed in contracted commercial hotels, chosen from competing proposals.

(total 401 beds)

notices.short_title: Integrated Commercial Hotels Program
notices.description:
The Department of Homeless Services (DHS') is seeking appropriately qualified contractors/vendors to contract for the provision of shelter services for families with children, adult families, and single adults who are temporarily housed in DHS contracted commercial hotels. The selected vendors will provide services as outlined in this RFP to assist clients with their daily needs and to help them move out of the shelter system as quickly as possible.

The mission of DHS is to prevent homelessness when possible and to provide short-term emergency shelter for individuals and families who have no other housing options available. DHS primarily meets this goal by providing services to clients in long-term contracted purpose-built shelters throughout the City. When there are not enough available shelter beds and units in traditional shelters, DHS temporarily uses commercial hotels to house clients while they transition to permanent housing.  

Over the last 15 years, DHS has faced numerous crises which have forced DHS to rely on commercial hotels to temporarily house clients. Long term DHS is committed to phasing out the use of commercial hotels.  However, until such time t…
notices.plain: The Department of Homeless Services awarded Urban Strategies Inc a $58,251,184 contract, selected from competing proposals, to provide shelter services for families, adult families and single adults housed temporarily in city-contracted commercial hotels.

notices.short_title: Immediate Emergency Demolition - 2592 3rd Ave, BX
notices.plain: The Department of Housing Preservation and Development awarded Statewide Demolition Corp an $850,000 emergency contract, bought without the usual competition, for demolition at 2592 3rd Ave. in the Bronx.

notices.short_title: Rental of Heavy Equipment Rental for Central Forestry Tree Planting Project
notices.plain: The Department of Parks and Recreation awarded United Rentals North America Inc. a $28,460 contract for heavy equipment rental for a central forestry tree planting project, through an intergovernmental purchase, meaning a contract another government already holds.

notices.short_title: FY27 SONYC Pilot NAE
notices.description: SONYC pilot program services middle school youth in ACS and homeless facilities. There are Pilots programs that are located at DHS, Secure Detention (SD) and Non-Secure Detention Facilities (NSD) providing support and services to youth involved in justice system. In collaboration with the Administration for Children Services and the Department of Homeless Services as well as community- based organizations with history working with these populations, DYCD offers tailored programming to cultivate supportive relationships, work with adolescents to stay on track, and foster optimism.
notices.plain: The Department of Youth and Community Development awarded CAMBA Inc a $708,933 contract through a negotiated acquisition to run the SONYC pilot program, which offers middle school youth in city child welfare, homeless and juvenile detention facilities with tailored support and mentoring.

notices.short_title: Summer Youth Employment Program NAQ
notices.vendor_name: Child Development Center of the Mosholu-Montefiore
notices.description: Summer Youth Employment Program (SYEP) providers through a variety of program models, serves youth ages 14-24 throughout New York City by providing opportunities to become familiar with the world of work, gain employment experience, and identify educational pathways that support career and life goals. This program is integral to the Citys workforce development strategy and provides a critical intervention point for underserved youth population.
notices.plain: The Department of Youth and Community Development awarded a $2.6 million contract to Child Development Center of the Mosholu-Montefiore through negotiation with one vendor to run the Summer Youth Employment Program, which gives New Yorkers ages 14 to 24 work experience and career planning.

notices.short_title: FY27 Beacon Program NAE
notices.description: DYCDs Beacon programs are collaborative, school-based community centers designed to provide quality services to youth and adults after school, in the evenings, and on weekends. The Beacons represent a unique convergence of youth and community development, through an integrated range of services, provided in an educational environment, and tailored to local needs.
notices.plain: The Department of Youth and Community Development awarded St. Vincent's Services Inc a $2.6 million negotiated contract, without open competition, to run a Beacon community center providing after-school, evening and weekend services for youth and adults.

notices.short_title: Summer Youth Employment NAQ
notices.description: Summer Youth Employment Program (SYEP) providers through a variety of program models, serves youth ages 14-24 throughout New York City by providing opportunities to become familiar with the world of work, gain employment experience, and identify educational pathways that support career and life goals. This program is integral to the Citys workforce development strategy and provides a critical intervention point for underserved youth population.
notices.plain: The Department of Youth and Community Development awarded Rockaway Development Revitalization Corp a $1.8 million contract, through negotiation among pre-qualified vendors, to run Summer Youth Employment Program services for youth ages 14 to 24.
